attribution.note: Marcus's own prediction in his signed open letter. He says it was adapted from work with Ernie Davis, but he states and endorses it.

semantics.note: An unhedged 'will not' with a 2029 horizon is a scored forecast. Dropping the Wozniak parenthetical does not change what he committed to.

contract.note: The plain reading (embodied competent cooking in varied ordinary kitchens, no teleoperation or bespoke installation) is fair and ordinary. Using 2029-12-31 as the deadline matches 'In 2029'.

evidence.note: YORI cooks autonomously, but in a structured kitchen with custom tools and appliances. That is not an arbitrary kitchen, so the early-resolution rule is not met.
Figure's own disclosure (Sept 2026) covers zero-shot tests in unseen homes, but for tidying, bed-making and towel folding, not cooking.

reviews.rationale: The deadline (end of 2029) is after the evaluation date. Neither item shows independently observed end-to-end cooking across varied unfamiliar kitchens, so the early contradiction rule is not triggered. The forecast cannot be scored yet.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his signed post.

semantics.note: Keeps 'really' and the open-ended 'and so forth'. It is a causal claim: debugging is hard because of limited understanding and a lack of targeted fixes.

contract.note: Splitting the difficulty claim from the explanation is reasonable. The result depends on whether one targeted research repair counts against 'nobody knows how to fix'. Given his sweeping wording, that reading is defensible, but the speaker did not supply it.

evidence.note: A 2021 survey says debugging is harder for opaque deep models. That supports the difficulty claim and its link to opacity. It also reviews explanation-based remedies that already existed.
ROME (v1, Feb 2022, before the post) traced where facts are stored and edited them directly, without more data or layers. That counts against 'nobody knows how to fix' beyond those remedies.

reviews.rationale: The claim that debugging was hard and that opacity made it harder holds (e1). The absolute part, that nobody understood the mechanisms or knew fixes beyond more data or layers, is contradicted by targeted mechanism tracing and editing published before the post (e2). e1's survey of remedies points the same way.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his signed post.

semantics.note: Faithful: the long-tail problem makes it easy to underestimate how hard AI problems are. A general causal claim with no deadline.

contract.note: The plain reading (success on common cases leads people to underestimate rare-case difficulty) matches his context. The population and effect size are unspecified, as the contract flags.

evidence.note: A study of trust built through repeated success before rare failures. It measures overtrust in a simulated task, not beliefs about how hard AI development is.

reviews.rationale: The only item is a nearby overtrust study. It does not measure underestimation of AI problem difficulty or isolate the long-tail mechanism. Nothing in the packet supports or refutes the causal claim, so it is unresolved on this evidence.

attribution.note: Marcus's own 'absolutely guarantee', addressed to Musk and so about Tesla.

semantics.note: A firm forecast. Reading 'this year or next' as 2022 or 2023 and taking Tesla as the target follow from the context.

contract.note: Level 5 means no human supervision; shipping includes software activation. Both are ordinary, fair readings.

evidence.note: Tesla's 2022 annual filing calls Autopilot/FSD driver assistance with the driver responsible. That is below Level 5. This is a company disclosure, but the contract accepts filings.
Tesla's 2023 annual filing, issued in Jan 2024, still describes driver-assist systems with the driver responsible. That covers the end of the horizon.

reviews.rationale: The deadline (end of 2023) has passed. Both of Tesla's annual filings describe only driver-assist systems with the driver responsible, which is below Level 5. The packet shows no Level 5 customer delivery. The forecast came true.
